extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals / PR practitioners pitching exclusives to national (Tier 1) media
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for PR practitioners on pitching exclusive stories and coordinating multi-tier press-release strategies aimed at Tier 1 (national/global) outlets. Covers targeting, timing/embargo, subject-line format, assets, and when to pursue or avoid Tier 1 placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 1 definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Massive business, consumer, or news outlets — Forbes, WSJ, NYT, USA Today, CNN, Good Morning America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National/global audiences (20M+ people). Highest credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 2 definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Trade publications, strong industry-specific outlets, regional major papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High credibility for specific audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 3 definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Smaller trade, local outlets, niche blogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-tail coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive strategy definition
rubrics_metrics.description: An exclusive is the offer of news to one reporter who will publish first, giving them exclusive access to cover the news before (or with) the press release crossing the wire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to incentivize a high-profile outlet to run a story first; typically coordinated under embargo or with timing control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness data / evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics and journalist preferences cited as evidence for exclusives and relationship-based pitching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: exclusive stories get 42% more social media engagement vs. non-exclusive; 82% of journalists prefer working with PR contacts they know; Tier 1 journalists receive 300+ pitches on average. Use these data points to justify strategy and resourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line format for exclusive pitches
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead with "EXCLUSIVE:" or "EXCLUSIVE INSIDE:" followed by a compelling news hook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: "EXCLUSIVE: First AI-Powered Ocean Cleanup System Launches". Be explicit about exclusivity and convey the news angle immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing / lead time and embargo practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach reporters under embargo at least 2 weeks in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-week lead time allows for interviews, asset gathering, and fact-checking. Maintain embargo discipline to preserve trust and the exclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic targeting of outlets/reporters
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the appropriate outlet for the story and match the outlet's coverage focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know a reporter's beat history and provide what they specifically need. Personalize the approach and give reporters the specific angle, assets, or sources they typically use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-tier strategy — Single Major News Story sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: A recommended sequencing plan for one major news item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) Tier 1 exclusive (one outlet) → 2) Embargoed wire distribution → 3) Tier 2 follow-up → 4) Tier 3 coverage. Use exclusivity first to win a marquee placement, then broaden coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-tier strategy — Coordinated release
rubrics_metrics.description: An approach for coordinated distribution across multiple outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple outlets simultaneously with wire distribution; embargoed for a level playing field. Consider a press conference if the news is major.

rubrics_metrics.name: What Tier 1 outlets want — From press releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements Tier 1 outlets expect to see in a pitch/press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genuine exclusivity (not 'exclusive to 10 outlets'), original data, access to leadership, multimedia, documents/evidence, and a story angle rather than just an announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: What Tier 1 outlets want — From PR contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavioral and relational expectations from PR representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal relationships, reliability, quick response, honest answers, source connections, and no hype.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine exclusive offered
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer a true single-outlet exclusive (not an "exclusive to multiple outlets") to be taken seriously by Tier 1 reporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusivity must be real and credible; false or diluted exclusives erode trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter selection based on past work
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose the reporter to receive the exclusive based on their past coverage and beat fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research the reporter's history and tailor the pitch to align with their interests and prior stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story angle (not just news)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch a distinctive story angle rather than merely announcing facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier 1 outlets want a narrative or hook that makes the story compelling to a national audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia prepared
rubrics_metrics.description: Have multimedia assets ready (images, video, charts, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing high-quality assets increases the chance of pickup and richer coverage (photo/video-friendly packaging).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership available
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure leadership or spokespeople are available for interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely access to executives or experts is often required by Tier 1 outlets for depth and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-week lead time
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide at least two weeks' notice when offering an exclusive under embargo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lead time supports backgrounding, interviews, asset development, and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and enforce embargo agreements with reporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breaking embargoes damages relationships and undermines exclusives; ensure internal teams understand timing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents/evidence offered
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide supporting documents and evidence with the pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary documents increase trust and allow journalists to independently verify claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent verification possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer items or data that allow independent verification of claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier 1 outlets want claims that can be corroborated; include data sources, methodology, or third-party confirmations when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line includes "EXCLUSIVE:"
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly mark the email subject with "EXCLUSIVE:" (or "EXCLUSIVE INSIDE:").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make exclusivity obvious in inbox triage to increase open and consideration rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch personalized to reporter
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailor the pitch to the specific reporter, not a templated or mass approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference the reporter's prior work and explain why this story matters to them and their audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provides reporter scoop
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the reporter new information or a scoop that makes their story distinctive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters prioritize content that yields an exclusive angle or new reporting; deliver something they can't get elsewhere easily.

rubrics_metrics.name: No PR hype (avoid over-selling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the pitch factual and avoid hyperbolic marketing language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authenticity and restraint build credibility; hype turns off Tier 1 reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame the story with an authentic, humanized narrative rather than corporate-speak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A genuine narrative helps national outlets see broader relevance and audience resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing relationship cultivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Invest in long-term relationships with reporters beyond single pitches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 82% of journalists prefer working with PR contacts they know — relationship-building increases future success.

rubrics_metrics.name: When NOT to pursue Tier 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions under which Tier 1 outreach is inappropriate or unlikely to succeed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not pursue Tier 1 when the story has a local angle (use local Tier 2), is trade-specific (use trade Tier 2), you have limited time/resources, the news is not strong enough, or you do not have a genuine exclusive to offer.
